name: Côte d'Ivoire
summary: Abidjan's lagoon skyline, the rainforest at Taï, the basilica at Yamoussoukro, and Atlantic beaches west towards Grand-Béréby — the economic engine of francophone West Africa.
when: The main dry season, between two sets of rains.

entries.caption: Lagoons, Forest and the Atlantic
entries.description: A lagoon city, one of West Africa's last rainforests, and five hundred kilometres of Atlantic.
entries.subject: the Abidjan skyline across the Ébrié lagoon

entries.caption: Forest to Savanna
entries.description: Rainforest in the south-west, a lagoon coast, and savanna running north to Mali.
entries.subject: the Ébrié lagoon fringed with palms

entries.caption: Taï and Comoé
entries.description: Pygmy hippo and chimpanzees at Taï, and Comoé's savanna in the north-east.
entries.subject: dense rainforest canopy at Taï national park

entries.caption: Comoé
entries.description: One of the largest protected areas in West Africa, with elephant, buffalo and hippo.
entries.subject: open savanna and gallery forest at Comoé

entries.caption: Mount Nimba
entries.description: The Nimba range on the Guinea and Liberia border, at 1,752 metres, with its own species.
entries.subject: the grassy summit ridge of Mount Nimba

entries.caption: Man and the Waterfalls
entries.description: The falls around Man in the western hills, and the liana bridges strung above them.
entries.subject: a waterfall in the hills around Man

entries.caption: The Ébrié and the Bandama
entries.description: The lagoon system behind the coast, and the Bandama running the length of the country.
entries.subject: pirogues on the Ébrié lagoon at dusk

entries.caption: Assinie and Grand-Béréby
entries.description: Assinie's sandbar east of Abidjan, and the quieter Atlantic beaches to the west.
entries.subject: palms and surf on the beach at Assinie

entries.caption: Taï Rainforest
entries.description: One of the last blocks of primary rainforest in West Africa, and chimpanzees that use tools.
entries.subject: primary rainforest interior at Taï

entries.caption: Surf, Hike, Paddle
entries.description: Surf at Assinie, hiking the western hills, and pirogues through the lagoon.
entries.subject: surfers in the water off Assinie

entries.caption: Sixty Peoples
entries.description: Akan, Krou, Mandé and Gur — around sixty peoples inside one border.
entries.subject: a Baoulé mask dance in central Côte d'Ivoire

entries.caption: Baoulé, Senufo and Dan
entries.description: Baoulé weaving, Senufo sculpture, and Dan masks from the western hills.
entries.subject: Senufo carved figures on a workshop bench

entries.caption: Attiéké and Kedjenou
entries.description: Attiéké with grilled fish, and kedjenou slow-cooked in a sealed pot.
entries.subject: attiéké and grilled fish served at a maquis

entries.caption: Abissa and the Masks
entries.description: Abissa at Grand-Bassam in November, and the mask festivals of the western hills.
entries.subject: masked dancers at the Abissa festival in Grand-Bassam

entries.caption: Weaving and Carving
entries.description: Baoulé strip cloth, Korhogo painted cloth, and Dan masks carved for use rather than sale.
entries.subject: Korhogo cloth painted with mud pigment

entries.caption: Grand-Bassam
entries.description: The first colonial capital, on a sandbar between lagoon and ocean, and now a world site.
entries.subject: the colonial quarter of Grand-Bassam

entries.caption: Yamoussoukro
entries.description: A basilica larger than Saint Peter's, built in the founder's home village.
entries.subject: the basilica of Our Lady of Peace at Yamoussoukro

entries.caption: Abidjan
entries.description: The Plateau's towers, the Ébrié lagoon, and a nightlife the region measures itself against.
entries.subject: the towers of the Plateau district in Abidjan

entries.caption: Lagoon Colonial
entries.description: The wooden trading houses of Grand-Bassam, and Abidjan's tropical modernism.
entries.subject: a colonial trading house on the Grand-Bassam waterfront

entries.caption: Maquis at Night
entries.description: The open-air maquis — grill, music and a plastic chair — is the country's real institution.
entries.subject: a busy open-air maquis at night in Abidjan

entries.caption: Beach and Lagoon
entries.description: Assinie's sandbar has ocean on one side and calm lagoon on the other, which suits children.
entries.subject: children swimming on the lagoon side at Assinie

entries.caption: Surf and Hike
entries.description: Assinie's breaks, and the liana bridges and falls in the hills around Man.
entries.subject: a liana bridge strung across a river near Man

entries.caption: Assinie and Abidjan
entries.description: Lagoon villas at Assinie, and Abidjan hotels that serve the whole region's business.
entries.subject: a lagoon-side villa terrace at Assinie

entries.caption: Taï and the Chimpanzees
entries.description: Forty years of chimpanzee research at Taï, run with the villages around the park.
entries.subject: a researcher on a forest trail at Taï

entries.caption: Lagoon Light
entries.description: Pirogues on flat water at either end of the day, and a skyline behind them.
entries.subject: pirogues silhouetted on the lagoon at sunset

entries.caption: Man
entries.description: The western hills, with waterfalls, mask villages and a mountain nobody climbs.
entries.subject: the hills and forest around the town of Man

entries.caption: The Engine of the Region
entries.description: The largest economy in francophone West Africa, and the easiest of them to travel.
entries.subject: a coastal highway running west out of Abidjan
